rounds.highest_value_visible_defect: The interpolated K5 CONTACT -> K6 RELEASE bridge retained the contact marker while the hand had already begun retreating, muddying the exact instant when local limb braking becomes release/reversal.
rounds.concrete_correction: Remove the interpolated connector at the causal join. Hold authored K5 contact cleanly, then cut directly to authored K6 RELEASED_AFTER_CONTACT / local reversal while the root continues forward. Do not alter the body-overrun key geometry.

rounds.actual_render_inspection: PASS after same-body bridge mutation: K1 has a rear/down asymmetrical coil; K2 moves pelvis/root before striking hand; K4 preserves a visible precontact gap; K5 holds explicit target contact for four frames; K6 now cuts immediately to a released hand eight grid cells behind contact while root has advanced five grid cells, cleanly separating local limb reversal from continuing body inertia; K7/K8 visibly compress and catch that overrun on wide front support; K9/K11 preserve hand/shoulder lag; K10 overshoots torso behind pelvis; K12/K13 settle and re-enter at a displaced address. No contact marker persists after hand release, no reverse interpolation, no idle reset, and no generic causal bridge remains at the contact fork.

rounds.taste: Crooked rear coil, long committed line, hard contact freeze, abrupt hand snapback while the body keeps arriving, then an ugly deep catch and diagonal overshoot form distinct silhouettes rather than polite mannequin phases.
rounds.function: The causal thesis is readable without metadata: the hand reverses first, the pelvis/root overruns, front support absorbs the remaining momentum, and the shoulder/hand repay debt later.
rounds.contempt: Recovery refuses the cheap reverse-playback solution: the body collapses through the spent strike, lags unevenly, overshoots, and returns action-ready while still displaced.
